problem.text: In triangle $ABC$, $AC = CD$ and $\angle CAB - \angle ABC = 30$ degrees. What is $\angle BAD$?

steps.title: Where to start: name the unknown angle
steps.body: We are told only the difference of two angles, not the angles themselves. That is a hint to name one of them with a letter and write the other in terms of it. Let $\angle ABC = b$; then $\angle CAB = b + 30$.

your_turn.prompt: Use the angle sum of triangle $ABC$ to write $\angle ACB$ in terms of $b$.

steps.title: Use the isosceles triangle $ACD$
steps.body:
Since $AC = CD$, triangle $ACD$ is isosceles. Careful: the equal angles are the ones opposite the equal sides, so $\angle CAD = \angle CDA$, not the angle at $C$. The angle at $C$ is $\angle ACD$, which is the same as $\angle ACB = 150 - 2b$ because $D$ lies on $CB$.
$$2\,\angle CAD + (150 - 2b) = 180$$

your_turn.prompt: Solve for $\angle CAD$ in terms of $b$.

steps.title: Split the angle at $A$
steps.body: Segment $AD$ cuts the angle at $A$ into two pieces. We know the whole angle and one piece in terms of $b$, so the other piece is their difference.

your_turn.answer: $D$ is on side $BC$, so ray $AD$ lies inside $\angle CAB$ and splits it into $\angle CAD$ and $\angle DAB$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: $\angle BAD = (b + 30) - (b + 15) = 15$. The unknown $b$ cancels, so the answer does not depend on the exact shape of the triangle. The answer is **$15^\circ$**.
